Page iv
Introduction
This Service Problem Management API enables service providers to manage service related
issues within their service area. Service problems may originate from two sources:
• Service Providers, who may declare issues based on their own monitoring or customer
feedback.
• Infrastructure Providers (e.g., cloud or network providers), who notify event information to
the
service
providers.
The
event
information
includes
alarm
information,
performance
anomaly information, trouble ticket information, SLA violations, maintenance activities and
prediction information.
Service
providers
can
refer
the
service
problems
and
the
event
information
from
infrastructure providers and receive notifications when new service problems arise or when
the
status
of
existing
problems
changes.
This
functionality
allows
service
providers
to
detect
and
respond
to
service
issues
quickly
and
accurately,
improving
operational
efficiency and customer satisfaction.

Sample Use Cases
We
assume
following
situation:
There
are
Network
Provider
1
(NP1)
and
2
(NP2),
which
provide network infrastructure, and Cloud Provider 1, 2, which provides cloud infrastructure,
as
First
Bs.
Using
this
infrastructure,
Service
Provider
1
(SP1),
2
(SP2)
and
3
(SP3)
are
providing their services to their end-users as Middle Bs.
Use Case 1
When trouble happen in any resources of NW/Cloud Providers, Service Providers can know
if their services are affected or not. The specific use case is following:
1.
SPM
collects
configuration
information
of
services
provided
by
service
providers
in
advance using Product Inventory Management API, etc.
2.
Each of Middle Bs – Service Provider 1 (SP1), Service Provider 2 (SP2), Service Provider 3
(SP3) – registers the notification destination to SPM SPI.
3.
When a fault occurs, SPM receives a trouble ticket from the Network Provider 1 (NP1).
4.
SPM creates a Service Problem based on the Trouble Ticket.
5.
SPM notifies the Service Problem creation notification to Middle B (SP1, SP3) to notify
expected service impact, based on the configuration information collected in advance.
6.
When SPM receives a notification that the trouble ticket has changed to "In Progress"
state,
update
the
status
of
the
relevant
Service
Problem.
Notify
the
Service
Problem
state change notification to Middle B (SP1, SP3).

After

In order to request the analysis of this event, Middle B declares a new service problem.

Since the SPM administrator found that necessary detailed information was insufficient,
SPM administrator requests additional information about the behavior of the Middle B
side.
5.
SP1 collects the specified additional information and registers it.
6.
SPM administrator checks the additional information and accepts the Service Problem
(Problem 1).
7.
First B(NP1) registers a detected problem event to the trouble ticket and notice a new

The SPM administrator can associate and group multiple service problems so that service

1.
SPM receives an alarm from NP1 and creates a Service Problem based on it (Problem 1).

Support of polymorphism and extension
patterns
Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by
means
of
a
list
of
generic
meta-attributes
that
we
describe
below.
Polymorphism
in
collections
occurs
when
entities
inherit
from
base
entities,
for
instance
a
TypeAServiceProblem
and
TypeBServiceProblem
inheriting
properties
from
the
abstract
ServiceProblem entity.
Generic
support
of
polymorphism
and
pattern
extensions
is
described
in
the
TMF
API
Guidelines v5.0 Part 2 document.
The
@type
attribute
provides
a
way
to
represent
the
actual
class
type
of
an
entity.
For
example,
within
a
list
of
ServiceProblem
instances
some
may
be
instances
of
TypeAServiceProblem where other could be instances of TypeBServiceProblem. The @type
gives this information. All resources and sub-resources of this API have a @type attributes
that can be provided when this is useful.
The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance an RelatedParty
object)
to
explicitly
denote
the
actual
entity
type
of
the
referred
class.
Notice
that
in
reference
entities
the
@type,
when
used,
denotes
the
class
type
of
the
reference
itself,
such
as
ServiceRef
or
TroubleTicketRef,
and
not
the
class
type
of
the
referred
object.
However since reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in
reference objects.
The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined
properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.
The
@baseType
attribute
gives
a
way
to
provide
explicitly
the
base
of
class
of
a
given
resource that has been extended.

Page 6
RESOURCE MODEL
ServiceProblem status lifecycle
The state diagram below gives an overview of the allowed status changes
The following table provides the service problem status explanation:
Status
Definition
Acknowledged
The Service Problem is acknowledged by Service problem
handler.
Service Problem Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 7
Status
Definition
Rejected
The Service Problem was Rejected because of
• Invalid or inadequate information is provided
• Failes to meet the business rules with respect to the
service which consumer is raising a service problem against
• Is otherwise defective
InProgress
The service problem was validated by the service problem
handler and is being processed.
Held
Service problem handler is confirming further details
internally before completing a service problem.
Pending
Service problem handler is awaiting further confirmation on
details of a Fault from originator before it can progress the
Fault.
Resolved
The fault indicated in the service problem was corrected by
the service problem handler and acknowledgement is
awaited from its originator.
Closed
The service Problem’s originator has acknowledged the
‘Resolved’ state of the service problem, or the timeframe for
acknowledgement has passed without response from
service problem originator.
Cancelled
The service problem was cancelled due to the following
reasons:
• The service problem originator cancelled
• The service problem handler cancelled as the problem was
not related to the handler
• The service provider handler deemed that the problem
cannot be resolved (non-fixable problem)
ProblemGroup and ProblemUngroup status lifecycle
ProblemGroup and ProblemUngroup operations follow the Task lifecycle model, with states
including acknowledged, rejected, inProgress, cancelled, done and terminatedWithError

ExternalIdentifier sub-resource fields
An identification of an entity that is owned by or originates in a software system different
from
the
current
system,
for
example
a
ProductOrder
handed
off
from
a
commerce
platform
into
an
order
handling
system.
The
structure
identifies
the
system
itself,
the
nature
of
the
entity
within
the
system
(e.g.
class
name)
and
the
unique
ID
of
the
entity
within the system. It is anticipated that multiple external IDs can be held for a single entity,
e.g. if the entity passed through multiple systems on the way to the current system. In this
case
the
consumer
is
expected
to
sequence
the
IDs
in
the
array
in
reverse
order
of
provenance, i.e. most recent system first in the list.
externalIdentifierType
A String. Type of the identification, typically would be the
type of the entity within the external system.
id
A String [1]. Identification of the entity within the external
system.
owner
A String. Name of the external system that owns the
entity.

GeographicLocation sub-resource fields
A GeographicLocation is a pure-virtual super-class to the GeoJSON-aligned geometries of
Point (addresses and locations), MultiPoint, LineString (streets, highways and boundaries),
MultiLineString and Polygon (countries, provinces, tracts of land). Use the @type attribute
to specify which of these is being specified by the geometry attribute.
bbox
A bbox. A bounding box array that contains the geometry.
The axes order follows the axes order of the geometry.
description
A String. Additional information of a user-friendly
description of the Place.

CalendarPeriod sub-resource fields
The CalendarPeriod schema represents a period of time within a calendar, defining various
attributes such as the applicable day, timezone, hour period, and status. It is designed to
capture information about the availability or status of a calendar period, which can be used
in scheduling, booking, or resource allocation applications.

week. ENUMERATED with values:
* mon
* tue
* wed
* thu
* fri
* sat
* sun
* weekdays
* weekend
hourPeriod
A HourPeriod [0..*]. Start and end time range in 24-hour
HH:mm format.

GeographicSubAddress sub-resource fields
Representation of a GeographicSubAddress It is used for addressing within a property in an
urban area (country properties are often defined differently). It may refer to a building, a
building cluster, or a floor of a multistory building.
buildingName
A String. Allows for buildings that have well-known names.
href
A String. Link to the subAddress.
id
A String. Unique Identifier of the subAddress.
levelNumber
A String. Used where a level type may be repeated e.g.
BASEMENT 1, BASEMENT 2.
levelType
A String. Describes level types within a building.
name
A String. Name of the subAddress to identify it with a
meaningful identification.
privateStreetName
A String. Private streets internal to a property (e.g. a
university) may have internal names that are not recorded
by the land title office.

ServiceProblemEventRecord resource
ServiceProblemEventRecord is a record of an event (related to a service problem) received
from another system. It is a system-generated record that captures events related to a
ServiceProblem,
such
as
status
changes,

serviceProblem
A ServiceProblem_EVO [1]. A Service Problem is an
indication that a service is no longer functioning according
to the agreement with its client(s). It is a condition where
a service fails to meet its expected performance,
availability, or quality standards, resulting in a negative
impact on the customer experience or business
operations.
ServiceProblem_EVO can be instantiated as
* ServiceProblem
ServiceProblem_EVO sub-resource fields
A Service Problem is an indication that a service is no longer functioning according to the
agreement
with
its
client(s).
It
is
a
condition
where
a
service
fails
to
meet
its
expected
performance,
availability,
or
quality
standards,

a
negative
impact
on

customer experience or business operations.
affectedLocation
A RelatedPlaceRefOrValue_EVO [0..*]. A list of the
locations affected by the problem. At least one of
affectedResource, affectedService or affectedLocation
should be present.
affectedNumberOfServices
An Integer. Number of affected services.
affectedResource
A ResourceRef_EVO [0..*]. A list of the resources affected
by the problem. At least one of affectedResource,
affectedService or affectedLocation should be present.
affectedService
A ServiceRef_EVO [0..*]. List of affected services. At least
one of affectedResource, affectedService or affected
Location should be present.
category
A String. Classifier for the problem. Settable. For example,
this is used for distinguish the category of problem
originator in [role].[category] format. Example: service
Provider.declarer, supplier.originated, system.originated.
characteristic
A Characteristic_EVO [0..*]. A list of additional properties/
data items that describe or characterize this service
problem. Please note that this list is currently
unconstrained but in a future version this property might
be constrained by a specification or deprecated
altogether.
Service Problem Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 72
creationDate
A DateTime. Time the problem was created.
description
A String. Free form text describing the Service Problem.
errorMessage
An ErrorMessage_EVO [0..*]. A list of the error(s)
associated to the Service Problem. This object is used for
any asynchronous errors and error information to be
shared with consumer.
externalIdentifier
An ExternalIdentifier_EVO [0..*]. A list of external
identifiers assoicated with this problem.
firstAlert
A RelatedEntity_EVO. A reference to an entity, where the
type of the entity is not known in advance.
href
A String. Hyperlink reference.
id
A String. Unique identifier.
impactImportanceFactor
An Integer. Impact Importance is characterized by an
Impact Importance Factor: overall importance of the
impact of all the affected services, e.g. 0 (zero impact) to
100 (worst impact). The Impact Importance is a calculated
field which is set by the OSS determining the impact.
impactPattern
An ImpactPattern_EVO. ImpactPattern is a used to
capture the nature and scope of the impact caused by a
Service Problem. It is used to describe how a service
problem affects other services or components, especially
when the impact cannot be fully captured by predefined
attributes.
lastUpdate
A DateTime. Time the problem was last changed.
name
A String. Name of the Service Problem.
note
A Note_EVO [0..*]. A list of comments or notes made on
the problem.
originatingSystem
A String. Indicates in which system the problem was
generated. Example: CRM Systems, Assurance System,
etc.
originatorParty
A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef_EVO. A reference to a
Party or PartyRole playing a specific role in context of the
entity to which it is related.
originatorResource
A ResourceRefOrResourceRoleRef_EVO. Resource
reference. A reference to a Resource or to the role that a
resource plays in a specific context.
Service Problem Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 73
parentProblem
A ServiceProblemRef_EVO [0..*]. The parent problem to
which this problem is attached.
priority
An Integer. An indication varying from 1 (highest) to 10
(lowest) of how important it is for the service provider to
correct the Service Problem.
problemEscalation
An Integer. Indicates if this service problem has been
escalated or not. Possible values are 0 to 10. A value of
zero means no escalation. The meanings of values 1-10 are
to be determined by the user of the interface, but they
show increasing levels of escalation.
reason
A String. Reason, if known, for the service problem that will
assist the Service Provider in understanding the
underlying cause or contributing factors, enabling more
accurate diagnosis and resolution. This can be set to
Unknown, otherwise.
relatedEntity
A RelatedEntity_EVO [0..*]. List of entities associated with
this problem. Example: Reference to TroubleTicket, Alarm
etc.
relatedEvent
An EventRef_EVO [0..*]. List of events associated to this
problem.
relatedParty
A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef_EVO [0..*]. List of
parties or party roles playing a role within the service
problem.
resolutionDate
A DateTime. Time the problem was resolved.
responsibleParty
A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef_EVO. A reference to a
Party or PartyRole playing a specific role in context of the
entity to which it is related.
rootCauseResource
A ResourceRef_EVO [0..*]. Resource(s) that are
associated to the underlying service problems that are
the Root Cause of this one if any (used only if applicable).
rootCauseService
A ServiceRef_EVO [0..*]. Service(s) that are associated to
the underlying service problems that are the Root Cause
of this one if any (used only if applicable).
slaViolation
A SLAViolationRef_EVO [0..*]. A List of SLA violations
associated with this problem.

status
A ServiceProblemStateType. The life cycle status of the
service problem, such as acknowledged, rejected,
inProgress, resolved etc… ENUMERATED with values:
* acknowledged
* rejected
* pending
* held
* inProgress
* resolved
* cancelled
* closed
statusChangeDate
A DateTime. Time the problem was last status changed.
statusChangeReason
A String. The reason of state change.
trackingRecord
A TrackingRecord_EVO [0..*]. List of tracking records that
allow the tracking of modifications on the problem.The
tracking records should not be embedded in the problem
to allow retrieving the problem without the tracking
records.
troubleTicket
A TroubleTicketRef_EVO [0..*]. A list of trouble tickets
associated with this problem.
underlyingAlarm
A ResourceAlarmRef_EVO [0..*]. A list of alarms underlying
this problem.
underlyingProblem
A ServiceProblemRef_EVO [0..*]. A list of underlying
problems. Relevant only if this problem is derived from
other problems.

ServiceProblem sub-resource fields
A Service Problem is an indication that a service is no longer functioning according to the
agreement
with
its
client(s).
It
is
a
condition
where
a
service
fails
to
meet
its
expected
performance,
availability,
or
quality
standards,
resulting
in
a
negative
impact
on
the
customer experience or business operations.
affectedLocation
A RelatedPlaceRefOrValue [0..*]. A list of the locations
affected by the problem. At least one of affected
Resource, affectedService or affectedLocation should be
present.
affectedNumberOfServices
An Integer. Number of affected services.
Service Problem Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 99
affectedResource
A ResourceRef [0..*]. A list of the resources affected by
the problem. At least one of affectedResource, affected
Service or affectedLocation should be present.
affectedService
A ServiceRef [0..*]. List of affected services. At least one of
affectedResource, affectedService or affectedLocation
should be present.
category
A String. Classifier for the problem. Settable. For example,
this is used for distinguish the category of problem
originator in [role].[category] format. Example: service
Provider.declarer, supplier.originated, system.originated.
characteristic
A Characteristic [0..*]. A list of additional properties/data
items that describe or characterize this service problem.
Please note that this list is currently unconstrained but in
a future version this property might be constrained by a
specification or deprecated altogether.
Characteristic can be instantiated as
* BooleanArrayCharacteristic
* BooleanCharacteristic
* FloatCharacteristic
* IntegerArrayCharacteristic
* IntegerCharacteristic
* NumberArrayCharacteristic
* NumberCharacteristic
* ObjectArrayCharacteristic
* ObjectCharacteristic
* StringArrayCharacteristic
* StringCharacteristic
creationDate
A DateTime. Time the problem was created.
description
A String [1]. Free form text describing the Service Problem.
errorMessage
An ErrorMessage [0..*]. A list of the error(s) associated to
the Service Problem. This object is used for any
asynchronous errors and error information to be shared
with consumer.
externalIdentifier
An ExternalIdentifier [0..*]. A list of external identifiers
assoicated with this problem.
firstAlert
A RelatedEntity. A reference to an entity, where the type
of the entity is not known in advance.
Service Problem Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 100
href
A String. Hyperlink reference.
id
A String. Unique identifier.
impactImportanceFactor
An Integer. Impact Importance is characterized by an
Impact Importance Factor: overall importance of the
impact of all the affected services, e.g. 0 (zero impact) to
100 (worst impact). The Impact Importance is a calculated
field which is set by the OSS determining the impact.
impactPattern
An ImpactPattern. ImpactPattern is a used to capture the
nature and scope of the impact caused by a Service
Problem. It is used to describe how a service problem
affects other services or components, especially when the
impact cannot be fully captured by predefined attributes.
lastUpdate
A DateTime. Time the problem was last changed.
name
A String. Name of the Service Problem.
note
A Note [0..*]. A list of comments or notes made on the
problem.
originatingSystem
A String. Indicates in which system the problem was
generated. Example: CRM Systems, Assurance System,
etc.
originatorParty
A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef. A reference to a Party
or PartyRole playing a specific role in context of the entity
to which it is related.
originatorResource
A ResourceRefOrResourceRoleRef. Resource reference. A
reference to a Resource or to the role that a resource
plays in a specific context.
parentProblem
A ServiceProblemRef [0..*]. The parent problem to which
this problem is attached.
priority
An Integer [1]. An indication varying from 1 (highest) to 10
(lowest) of how important it is for the service provider to
correct the Service Problem.
problemEscalation
An Integer. Indicates if this service problem has been
escalated or not. Possible values are 0 to 10. A value of
zero means no escalation. The meanings of values 1-10 are
to be determined by the user of the interface, but they
show increasing levels of escalation.
Service Problem Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 101
reason
A String [1]. Reason, if known, for the service problem that
will assist the Service Provider in understanding the
underlying cause or contributing factors, enabling more
accurate diagnosis and resolution. This can be set to
Unknown, otherwise.
relatedEntity
A RelatedEntity [0..*]. List of entities associated with this
problem. Example: Reference to TroubleTicket, Alarm etc.
relatedEvent
An EventRef [0..*]. List of events associated to this
problem.
relatedParty
A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef [0..*]. List of parties or
party roles playing a role within the service problem.
resolutionDate
A DateTime. Time the problem was resolved.
responsibleParty
A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef. A reference to a Party
or PartyRole playing a specific role in context of the entity
to which it is related.
rootCauseResource
A ResourceRef [0..*]. Resource(s) that are associated to
the underlying service problems that are the Root Cause
of this one if any (used only if applicable).
rootCauseService
A ServiceRef [0..*]. Service(s) that are associated to the
underlying service problems that are the Root Cause of
this one if any (used only if applicable).
slaViolation
A SLAViolationRef [0..*]. A List of SLA violations associated
with this problem.
status
A ServiceProblemStateType. The life cycle status of the
service problem, such as acknowledged, rejected,
inProgress, resolved etc… ENUMERATED with values:
* acknowledged
* rejected
* pending
* held
* inProgress
* resolved
* cancelled
* closed
statusChangeDate
A DateTime. Time the problem was last status changed.
statusChangeReason
A String. The reason of state change.

the tracking of modifications on the problem.The tracking
records should not be embedded in the problem to allow

troubleTicket
A TroubleTicketRef [0..*]. A list of trouble tickets
associated with this problem.
underlyingAlarm
A ResourceAlarmRef [0..*]. A list of alarms underlying this
problem.
underlyingProblem

Relevant only if this problem is derived from other
problems.

ProblemGroup resource
Task resource that requests Service Problems to be grouped together into a parent and set
of
children.
The
problemGroup
task
is
used
to
group
related
service
problems
under
a
common parent problem so as to enable logical grouping of related issues that may share a
common root cause or require coordinated resolution. This improves operational efficiency
by consolidating related problems, enhances visibility across incidents, simplifies tracking
and reporting, and supports clearer communication among stakeholders. Depending on the
implementor’s
design,
the
problemGroup
task
may
support
partial
updates,
allowing
selective removal of some child problems while retaining others.

ProblemUngroup resource
Task resource that requests Service Problems to be ungrouped from a parent. The problem
Ungroup task is used to disassociate child service problems from a parent problem within a
problemGroup.
This
operation
breaks
the
logical
grouping,
allowing
individual
service
problems to be managed independently. For example, it can be applied in the scenarios
where the relationship between problems is no longer valid, OR the root cause has been
resolved and individual issues need separate handling etc. Depending on the implementor’s
design, partial ungrouping could be supported. The task can target specific child problems
for
removal
while
leaving
others
intact
to
allow
flexible
and
selective
updates
to
the
problem group structure.

•

Notifications related to ProblemGroup:
•

The notification structure for all notifications in this API follow the pattern depicted by the
figure below. A notification event resource (depicted by "SpecificEvent" placeholder) is a
sub class of a generic Event structure containing at least an id of the event occurrence
(eventId), an event timestamp (eventTime), and the name of the resource (eventType). This
notification
structure
owns
an
event
payload
structure
("SpecificEventPayload"
placeholder) linked to the resource concerned by the notification using the resource name
as access field ("resourceName" placeholder).

Description
Query Entities

a representation of a
resource.
Create Entity
POST Resource

a new resource
Partial Update of an Entity
PATCH Resource
PATCH must be used to
partially update a resource
Remove an Entity
DELETE Resource
DELETE must be used to
remove a resource
Execute an Action on an
Entity

POST must be used to
execute Task Resources
Other Request Methods
POST on TASK Resource
GET and POST must not be
used to tunnel other request
methods.

API NOTIFICATIONS
For
every
single
of
operation
on
the
entities
use
the
following
templates
and
provide
sample REST notification POST calls.
It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in
the REST Guidelines reproduced below.
Register listener
POST /hub
Description
Sets
the
communication
endpoint
address
the
service
instance
must
use
to
deliver
information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST
calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case
DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.
Request
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
 
"callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
Response
201
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42

Unregister listener
DELETE /hub/{id}
Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.

Accept: application/json

204
